▪ Electricity is working, but the mechanics and plumbing are not.

▪ The absence of a palpable pulse and absence of myocardial muscle activity with 
presence of organized electrical activity on the cardiac monitor. The patient is clinically dead despite some type of organized rhythm on monitor.

slides.title: Overview of Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) Syndrome
slides.content:
Overview of Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) Syndrome

WPW Syndrome refers to the presence of a congenital accessory pathway (AP) and episodes of tachyarrhythmias. The term is often used interchangeablely with pre-excitation syndrome.

First described in 1930 by Louis Wolff, John Parkinson and Paul Dudley White.

Incidence is 0.1 – 3.0 per 1000

Associated with a small risk of sudden cardiac death

slides.title:
• Sinus rhythm with a very short PR interval (< 120 ms)

• Broad QRS complexes with a slurred upstro
slides.content:
• Sinus rhythm with a very short PR interval (< 120 ms)

• Broad QRS complexes with a slurred upstroke to the QRS complex — the delta wave

• Dominant R wave in V1 suggests a left-sided AP, and is sometimes referred to as “Type A” WPW

• Tall R waves and inverted T waves in V1-3 mimicking right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH) — these changes are due to WPW and do not indicate underlying RVH
• Negative delta wave in aVL simulating the Q waves of lateral infarction — this is referred to as the “pseudo-infarction” pattern

slides.title:
• Sinus rhythm with very short PR interval (< 120 ms)

• Broad QRS complexes with a slurred upstroke
slides.content:
• Sinus rhythm with very short PR interval (< 120 ms)

• Broad QRS complexes with a slurred upstroke to the QRS complexes — the delta wave

• Dominant S wave in V1 indicates a right-sided AP — sometimes referred to as “Type B” WPW

• Tall R waves and inverted T waves in the inferior leads and V4-6 mimic the appearance of left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) — again, this is due to WPW and does not indicate underlying LVH.

slides.title: Ventricular rhythms
slides.content:
Ventricular rhythms

• When the sinoatrial (SA) node and the AV Junctional tissues fails to generate an 
impulse the ventricles will assume the role of pacing the heart.

• There is an absence of P waves because there is no atrial activity or depolarization.

• Ventricular rhythms will display QRS complexes that are wide (greater than or equal to 120 milliseconds) and bizarre in appearance.

slides.title: Ventricular rhythms
slides.content:
Ventricular rhythms

This is rhythm initiated at the level of the ventricules, also known as ideal ventricular rhythm or idioventricular rhythm or ventricular escape rhythm. The resting rate is 20 to 40/minutes.



Keys to identifying: rhythm is SLOW, no P wave, wide & bizarre QRS!

slides.title: Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm (AIVR)
slides.content:
Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm (AIVR)

Accelerated idioventricular arrhythmia is last-ditch effort of the ventricles to try to prevent cardiac standstill.

• SA node and AV node have failed 
• Rate usually between 40 to 120 beats per minute (bpm)

slides.title: VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA
slides.content:
VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA

▪ Ventricular tachycardia almost always occurs in diseased hearts. 

▪ Rhythm in which three or more PVCs arise in sequence at a rate greater than 150 beats per 
minute and above.

▪ V-tach can quickly deteriorate into ventricular fibrillation. The causes includes ischemia heart disease and cardiomyopathy.

• Antiarrhythmics drugs such as Amiodaron are used to restore nomal heart rate.

VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION

Ventricular fibrillation (VF) is the most important shockable cardiac arrest rhythm.

Rate: 300 to 500bpm.

The ventricles suddenly attempt to contract at rates of up to 500 bpm

Agonal Rhythm

Agonal rhythm is when the Idioventricular rhythm is 20 beats or less per minute. Frequently is seen as the last-ordered semblance of a heart rhythm when resuscitation efforts are unsuccessful.

slides.title: TORSADE DE POINTES
slides.content:
TORSADE DE POINTES

It is an uncommon and distinctive form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT).
It is often referred as torsade and is associated with prolong QT interval
TDP starts in the heart’s lower chamber (ventricle)
Characterized by gradual change in the amplitude and twisting of the QRS complex around isoelectric line.
It may be acquired or congenital. 
TDP may degenerate into ventricular fibrillation (VT).

slides.title: JUNCTIONAL RHYTHM
slides.content:
JUNCTIONAL RHYTHM

A JUCTIONAL RHYTHM OCCURS WHEN THE HEART’S ELECTRICAL IMPULSES ORIGINATE FROM THE AV JUNCTION(AV NODE AREA) INSTEAD OF THE SA NODE.
IT ARISES WHEN THE SA NODE FAILS OR WHEN THE CONDUCTION FRON THE ATRIAL IS BLOCKED
RATE IS BETWEEN 40-60BPM(INTINSIC RATE OF THE AV NODE)
SLOWER THAN SINUS RHYTHM.
P WAVES OFTEN ABSENT,INVERTED,OR RETROGRADE(AFTER QRS COMPLEX).
QRS COMPLEX IS OF A NORMAL WIDTH
PR INTERVAL IS SHORT IF P WAVE IS PRESENT OR ABSENT IF NO P WAVE.

slides.title: CAUSES OF JUNCTIONAL RHYTHM
slides.content:
CAUSES OF JUNCTIONAL RHYTHM

SA NODE DYSFUNCTION(E.G SICK SINUS SYNDROME).
MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION(ESPECIALLY INFERIOR WALL).
MEDICASTIONS E.G DIGOXIN TOXICITY,BETA BLOCKERS.
INCREASED VAGAL TONE.
ELECTROLYTE DISTURBANCES

slides.title: TYPES OF JUNCTIONAL RHYTHMS
slides.content:
TYPES OF JUNCTIONAL RHYTHMS

THEY ARE CLASSIFIED BASED ON HEARTRATE AND CLINICAL CONTEXT BUT THEY ALL ORIGINATE FROM THE AV JUNCTION.

slides.title: JUNCTIONAL ESCAPE RHYTHM
slides.content:
JUNCTIONAL ESCAPE RHYTHM

RATE IS BETWEEN 40-60BPM
IT COMES UP AS A RESULT OF THE TEMPORARY FAILURE OF THE SA NODE TO GENERATE IMPULSE
AFTER THE ESCAPE RHYTHM,YOU MIGHT HAVE A NORMAL SINUS RHYTHM .

slides.title: OTHERS ARE AS FOLLOWS
slides.content:
OTHERS ARE AS FOLLOWS

ACCELERATED JUNCTIONAL RHYTHM -RATE IS BETWEEN 60-100BPM

JUNCTIONAL TACHYCARDIA-RATE ABOVE 100BPM.

JUNCTIONAL BRADYCARDIA-RATE BELOW 40BPM.

PREMATURE JUNCTIONAL RHYTHM-RHYTHM IS IRREGULAR.IT OCCURS BEFORE THE NEXT NORMAL BEAT

slides.title: COMMON LEAD ERRORS
slides.content:
COMMON LEAD ERRORS

THE MOST COMMON ERROR THAT OCCURS DURING ECG RECORDING ARE MAJORLY THAT OF LIMB REVERSAL.
REVERSAL CAN BE LIMB LEAD OR CHEST LEAD AND THIS MIGHT LEAD TO A CHANGE IN THE MORPHOLOGY OF THE RECORDING IN WHICH CASE THE P,QRS OR T WAVES MIGHT BE REVERSED.
WHEN YOU HAVE ALL LEADS REVERSED THEN YOU HAVE GLOBAL LIMB LEAD INVERSION.
ELECTRICAL AXIS BECOMES ABNORMAL.

slides.title: LEAD ERRORS
slides.content:
LEAD ERRORS

IF THE CHEST LEADS ARE REVERSED ,THE ECG RECORDING FOR THE CHEST LEADS WILL BE AFFECTED

slides.title: BASIC ECG INTERPRETATION
slides.content:
BASIC ECG INTERPRETATION

HEARTRATE-THIS IS THE RATE AT WHICH THE HEART BEATS AND THE UNIT IS BEAT PER MINUTES(BPM).
NORMAL RATE IS BETWEEN 60-100bpm
The beat can be regular or irregular as such the calculation for the rate differs.
FOR EASY ECG  AND STEP BY STEP INTERPRETATION,THE FOLLOWING PATTERN MAY BE ADOPTED:
REGULAR RHYTHMS-
Here, the R-R intervals are consistent:
                      USING THE LARGE BOX METHOD
Count the number of large boxes between 2 successive R waves(R-R interval)
Divide it by 300 that is 300/number of large boxes
        e.g. Number of large boxes is 4,heartrate 300/4=75bpm

slides.title: HEART RATE
slides.content:
HEART RATE

SMALL BOX METHOD
Count the number of small squares between R-R waves
Divide your value by 1500 that is 1500/R-R interval
Eg if R-R is 20 small squares then rate =1500/20=75bpm
      6 SECONDS STRIP METHOD:
Though mostly used for irregular rhythm.
Count how many R waves in a 6 seconds strip(30 large boxes)
Multiply your value by 10 that gives you the heartrate 
E.g 7 R waves in 6seconds ,HR=7x10=70bpm

slides.title: HEART RATE
slides.content:
HEART RATE

IRREGULAR RHYTHM e.g Atrial fibrillation
Small or large box method cannot be used here
Use a large long strip especially lead II.
Count the number of QRS  in 
    6 seconds(30 boxes) on paper run at 25mm/s.
     Multiply the number by 10 to get heartbeat 
(6secx10=60sec=1min)
E.g say in 6-seconds you count 9 QRS complexes:
Heartrate =9x10=90bpm.

slides.title: HEARTRATE
slides.content:
HEARTRATE

1O seconds method .
1 large box =5mm=250 small boxes in 10 seconds
1 large box=5mm=250/5=50 large boxes in 10 seconds
In this method you count 50 large boxes and count the number of QRS in them and multiply by 6.
E.g heartrate 14 QRSx6=84bpm

slides.title: HEARTRATE
slides.content:
HEARTRATE

NORMAL HEARTRATE IS BETWEEN 60
RATE LESS THAN 60BPM IS BRADYCARDIA
RATE HIGHER THAN 100BPM IS TACHYCARDIA
TYPE OF BRADY OR TACHYCARDIA DEPENDS ON TYPE OF RHYTHM E.G SINUS TACHYCARDIA,ATRIAL TACHYCARDIA,V-TACH,JUNCTIONAL TACHYCARDIA ETC

slides.title: RHYTHM
slides.content:
RHYTHM

REGULAR RHYTHM IS ONE IN WHICH :
     The P waves is followed by a QRS complex which is in turned followed by a 
      T waves 
      The R-R interval is regular
      The P waves is upright in I,II,Avf.
       The rate is between 60-100bpm
       Normal PR interval (0.12-0.20sec)
       Narrow QRS ,about 0.10sec and less.
Note: Normal sinus rhythm shows that the SA Node started the cardiac excitation which is always represented by the presence of An upright P waves

slides.title: AXIS
slides.content:
AXIS

Axis provides information about the heart’s electrical orientation and can help identify underlying conditions.
It can be Normal or Abnormal
Simple way to determine the axis is to look at the QRS in lead I,IIand aVF.
If QRS in lead I and Avf is positive =NORMAL AXIS.
If lead I positive and Avf negative,check lead II
       If positive =normal axis
        If negative=left axis deviation.

slides.title: AXIS
slides.content:
AXIS

If lead I is negative and Avf is positive=RIGHT AXIS DEVIATION
If lead I is negative and avf is negat0oi[]98ukilo0;pive =EXTREME AXIS(rare)
Possible causes of LAD-left anterior fascicular hemi block, LVH, Inferior MI.
Possible causes of RAD-RVH, pulmonary conditions(PE,COPD),lateral MI
Possible causes of Extreme axis-severe ventricular rhythm disturbance, advance conduction block

slides.title: P  WAVES
slides.content:
P  WAVES

IT REPRESENTS ATRIAL DEPOLARIZATION
IT IS THE FIRST POSITIVE DEFLECTION ON AN ECG 
IT IS GENERATED WHEN THERE IS AN IMPULSE 
  FROM SA NODE.
THE NORMAL VALUE FOR THE P WAVE IS 
      0.08sec -12sec 
IT IS SMOOTH,ROUNDED.
UPRIGHT IN LEAD LEAD I, II, aVF; INVERTED IN Avr
BEST PLACE TO CHECK FOR P WAVES IS LEAD II 
  AND V1.
IN V1 IT IS MOSTLY BIPHASIC

slides.title: P WAVES
slides.content:
P WAVES

TO CALCULATE THE P WAVES YOU COUNT FROM BEGINNING OF THE P TO THE END THEN MULTIPLY BY THE CONSTANT 0.04.
NORMAL AMPLITUDE IS 2.5mm.
ABSENT P WAVES +IRREGULAR RHYTHM=ATRIAL FIBRILLATION
LONG P WAVES>0.12sec(LAE) AND “m” PATTERNED P WAVES (P-MITRALE) OR AMPLITUDE MORE THAN 2.5MM (RAE OR P-PULMONALE).
ABSENT, INVERTED( BEFORE, HIDDEN OR AFTER QRS) IS JUNCTIONAL OR NODAL RHYTHM
SA TOOTH APPEARANCE=ATRIAL FLUTTER
P WAVES UNRELATED TO QRS COMPLEXE=AV DISSOCIATION(COMPLETE HEART BLOCK)

slides.title: PR INTERVAL
slides.content:
PR INTERVAL

IT IS THE TIME BETWEEN THE BEGINNING OF THE P WAVES AND THE BEGINNING OF THE QRS COMPLEX.
IT IS THE INTERVAL BETWEEN THE BEGINNING OF ELECTRICAL EXCITATION OF THE ATRIAL AND THE BEGINNING OF EXCITATION OF THE VENTRICLE(SA NODE THROUGH THE ATRIUM,AV NODE,AND BUNDLE OF HIS TO THE VENTRICLES)
DURATION IS BETWEEN 0.12 - 0.20seconds
SHORT PR INTERVAL =WPW(WOLFF –PARKINSON-WHITE ) SYNDROME-ACCESSORY PATHWAY (BUNDLE OF KENT) OR LOWN-GANONG-LEVINE SYNDROME.
PROLONGED PR > 0.20SEC = 1ST DEGREE , 2ND DEGREE AV BLOCKS

slides.title: QRS COMPLEX
slides.content:
QRS COMPLEX

IT REPRESENTS VENTRICULAR DEPOLARIZATION (BY PURKINJE FIBRES)
NORMAL DURATION 0.06 - 0.10SEC
PROLONGED QRS>0.12SEC = BUNDLE BRANCH BLOCK,VENTRICULAR RHYTHM,HYPERKALEMIA
TALL QRS = VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY, ATHLETE HEART.
LOW QRS = PERICARDIA EFFUSION, OBESITY, COPD
ABNORMAL Q WAVES = MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION IF IT IS DEEP AND WIDE

slides.title: ST SEGMENT
slides.content:
ST SEGMENT

IT AN ISOELECTRIC POINT WHERE NO ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY OCCURS.
IT SHOWS THE POINT BETWEEN VENTRICULAR DEPOLARIZATION AND REPOLARIZATION
ABNORMAL ST SEGMENT CAN BE AN ELEVATED ONE SEEN IN S.T.E.M.I OR DEPRESSION IN N.S.T.E.M.I; DOWNSLOPPING AS SEEN IN ISCHEMIA OR STRAIN PATTERN

slides.title: ST SEGMENTS
slides.content: ST SEGMENTS

slides.title: QT INTERVAL
slides.content:
QT INTERVAL

IT REPRESENTS TOTAL TIME FOR VENTRICULAR DEPOLARIZATION AND REPOLARIZATION
ESSENTIALLY THE PERIOD FROM THE BEGINNING OF VENTRICULAR CONTRACTION TO THE END OF RECOVERY.
SPECIFICALLY REPRESENTS THE ELECTRICAL ACTIVITIES OF THE VENTRICLES.
IT IS <0.44SEC IN MALE AND <0.46SEC IN FEMALES
PROLONGED QT INTERVAL CAN INCREASE THE RISK OF DANGEROUS HEART RHYTHMS ABNORMALITIES SUCH ASN TORSADE DE PONTES A KIND OF V-TACH THAT CAN LEAD TO SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH.
SHORT QT INTERVAL <0.33-0.34SEC IS CONSIDERED SHORT.
SHORT QT IS NOT COMMON
IT MEANS THAT THE HEART IS REPOLARIZING FASTER THAN NORMAL
MAY CAUSE LIFE THREATENING ARRYTHMIAS SUCH AS V-FIBRILLATION OR SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH

slides.content: QT INTERVAL

slides.title: QTC
slides.content:
QTC

IT IS CORRECTED QT AND IT IS CALCULATED DUE TO THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN QT INTERVAL AND THE HEART RATE
IT ALLOWS FOR MORE ACCURATE ASSESSMENT OF THE QT INTERVAL.
CALCULATED USING BAZETT”S FORMULAR=QT/√R-R
NORMAL VALUE,MEN 0.35-0.445SEC,WOMEN0.35-0.46SEC.
<0.35SEC IS SHORT QTc
SAME EFFECT WITH LONG OR SHORT QT

slides.title: T WAVES
slides.content:
T WAVES

REPRESENTS VENTRICULAR REPOLARIZATION
TYPICALLY,A NORMAL T WAVES IS UPRIGHT IN MOST ECG LEADS EXCEPT aVR WHERE IT IS INVERTED
THERE ARE SOME ABNORMAL T WAVES:
PEAKED T WAVES SEEN IN HYPERKALEMIA
INVERTED T WAVES SEEN IN ISCHEMIA,PERICARDITIS,MYOCARDITIS ETC
BIPHASIC T WAVES –IT HAS BOTH POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE DEFLECTION.

slides.title: R WAVES
slides.content:
R WAVES

R WAVES IN THE PRECORDIAL LEADS (V1-V6).THE R WAVES NORMALLY INCREASES IN SIZE FROM V1 TO V4 OR V5 THEN DECREASES IN V6.
THIS IS KNOWN AS NORNAL R WAVES PROGRESSION.
A TALL R WAVES IN V1 CAN INDICATE RIGHT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY(RVH)
POOR R WAVES CAN SUGGEST M.I OR HYPERTROPHY

slides.title: S.T.E.M.I AND N.S.T.E.M.I(S.T ELEVATION MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION AND NON-S.T SEGMENT MYOCARDIAL INFARCT
slides.content:
S.T.E.M.I AND N.S.T.E.M.I(S.T ELEVATION MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION AND NON-S.T SEGMENT MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION)

It is a type of heart attack caused by a complete blockage of a coronary artery.It is a medical emergency that requires immediate attention.
STEMI is diagnosed primarily using ECG.Findings are:
       -Elevation of ST segment in two or more contiguous leads.
       -Threshold for diagnosis
           .>1mm in limb leads(I,II,III,aVL and aVF)  
            .>2mm in chest leads in men >40 years
            .>1.5mm in chest leads (V2-V3)
       -The elevation should be convex upwards or tombstone-shaped
       -Pathologic Q waves
            may develop later
            sign of irreversible myocardial necrosis.
        -T waves inversion
            may follow ST elevation as part of evolution

slides.title: STEMI
slides.content:
STEMI

Localizing the STEMI on ecg .
Anterior wall(V1-V4) LEFT ANTERIOR DESCENDING(LAD)
Lateral wall(I,AVL,V5 and V6)  LEFT CIRCUMFLEX(LCx)
Inferior wall (II,III and AVF.) RIGHT CORONARY ARTERY(RCA)
Posterior wall ST DEPRESSION IN V1-V3 RCA OR LCx(posterior branch)
